Photosynthesis.definition: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make their own food using light energy, carbon dioxide and water in the presence of chlorophyll.
key_ideas: Plants use light energy to make food.
Carbon dioxide enters the leaf from the air.
Water is absorbed from the soil and transported to the leaves.
Chlorophyll absorbs light energy.
Glucose is produced during photosynthesis.
Oxygen is released as a by-product.
examples: Green leaves exposed to sunlight can carry out photosynthesis.
A plant kept without sufficient light cannot photosynthesise effectively.

Chlorophyll.definition: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in plant cells that absorbs light energy needed for photosynthesis.
key_ideas: Chlorophyll gives many leaves their green colour.
It absorbs light energy.
The absorbed light energy is used during photosynthesis.
examples: Leaves with little or no chlorophyll have reduced ability to photosynthesise.

Carbon Dioxide.definition: Carbon dioxide is a gas from the air that green plants use as a raw material during photosynthesis.
key_ideas: Carbon dioxide enters leaves mainly through stomata.
It provides carbon needed to make glucose.
Carbon dioxide is one of the raw materials required for photosynthesis.
examples: A plant needs carbon dioxide from the surrounding air to photosynthesise.
Closing or blocking stomata can reduce carbon dioxide entering a leaf.

Water.definition: Water is a raw material for photosynthesis and is absorbed from the soil by plant roots before being transported to the leaves.
key_ideas: Roots absorb water from the soil.
Water is transported to the leaves through xylem vessels.
Water is used during photosynthesis.
examples: A plant without enough water cannot photosynthesise effectively.
Water absorbed by roots can reach the leaves through the stem.

Glucose.definition: Glucose is a sugar produced by plants during photosynthesis and can be used to provide energy or converted into other substances for growth and storage.
key_ideas: Glucose is produced during photosynthesis.
Glucose can be used in respiration to release energy.
Plants can convert glucose into starch for storage.
examples: Excess glucose in a plant may be stored as starch.
Glucose can be used by growing plant tissues.

Stomata.definition: Stomata are tiny openings, mainly found on the surfaces of leaves, that allow gases to move into and out of the leaf.
key_ideas: Carbon dioxide enters leaves through stomata.
Oxygen can leave the leaf through stomata.
Stomata are controlled by guard cells.
examples: Open stomata allow carbon dioxide to enter a leaf.
Stomata can close when a plant needs to reduce water loss.
